$note: Project config for scripts/conductor.mjs. Everything project-specific lives here — including the board's own location (boardPath) — so the conductor script is reusable across repos unchanged. Absent keys fall back to built-in defaults.
$verifyCommandsNote: P0-01 (EXECUTION_PLAN Law L1): the trust commands. Run by scripts/conductor/receipts.mjs mintReceipt() — never by the agent session — and written to docs/work/receipts/<ticket>-<sha12>.json with per-command exit codes. runGates() asserts the receipt; a pre-existing (possibly hand-edited) receipt is overwritten unread. Moved OUT of gates[] so they run exactly once, under attestation.
$mechanicalFixNote: P2-03: approved deterministic autofixes. When EVERY failed verify command matches a rule, ONE bounded remediation pass runs (out-of-scope touches reject the whole pass; the amendment is committed; gates re-run; no coding attempt consumed). eslint --fix and prettier --write are mechanical by construction; nothing here may waive security, delete tests, or weaken assertions.
gates: OUT=$(mktemp -d) && node apps/web/scripts/capture-acceptance.mjs gate --out "$OUT" >/dev/null && node scripts/validate-visual.mjs --run "$OUT"; rc=$?; rm -rf "$OUT"; exit $rc

validators.$note: gate[] = reliable/objective validators, run diff-scoped as HARD gates. advisory[] = grep-heuristic validators (noisy on TS: magic-numbers-in-comments, bogus-unreachable) — their findings ANCHOR the LLM review instead of blocking, matching the source system's 'script floor + agent verified pass' design. Promote a validator to gate[] once red-fixture-calibrated. repoWide[] (W10-49): findings from these are NOT filtered to the ticket diff. Only honest while the validator reports ZERO repo-wide — then any finding is necessarily something this ticket introduced. validate-file-size hit zero at W10-48 (six over-cap files cleared across W10-46/47/48); if that count ever goes non-zero again, every ticket fails for debt it did not create, so remove the entry rather than waiving it.

$exportsGateNote: W12-10, 2026-08-13: validate-exports.mjs joins the per-ticket gate as a RATCHET (--max 48), not a clean-zero check. It reports exported symbols that tests reference and production code never does — something built, verified, and wired to nothing. Baseline 48 is this repo's measured debt at filing; failing every ticket for it would be the exact mistake the repoWide note above warns about, so the gate only fires when the count EXCEEDS the baseline. Lower it whenever the number drops; never raise it to make a ticket pass. CALIBRATION MATTERS HERE and was done rather than assumed: the first draft reported 529 symbols (all exports, cross-package refs only), which is instantly waivable noise. Filtering to VALUE exports via the TS checker took it to 245 (a type nobody names is harmless; a function nobody calls is dead), counting references inside the declaring package took it to 135, and counting in-file uses beyond the declaration itself — the sibling-factory false positive, e.g. createMacKeychainCredentialStore called by resolveCredentialStore beside it — took it to 48. Same shape as attest v3.5.1s honest-denominator pass (71 -> 8). What it catches today includes loop:createToolAnchor (W12-05), the three cloud provider factories, and several pipeline verbs.

$barrelCountingNote: W12-39, 2026-08-18: --max raised 43 -> 62, and this is NOT the forbidden 'raise the baseline to make a ticket pass' — the rule that forbids that is about absorbing NEW debt a change created. Nothing was wired to nothing by this ticket; the counting got sharper and 19 symbols that were already dead stopped hiding. W12-10 counted a bare word-boundary match over raw file text and said so in its own module doc ('a comment mentioning a name reads as a use'), treating false negatives as the safe direction. W12-38 then measured what that concealed and found the check's own worst instance behind two prose mentions. Comments are now blanked for both passes, and the 19 newly visible symbols are: events promoteGlobalPlaybookEntry; gateway PRESET_ROLES, BudgetBreakerTracker; harbormaster runClaimLoop, createFileStopSwitch; loop runMicroLoop, phaseGatePasses, toCoverageReportJson, createStubMemoryAnchor, updateCalibration, gateDecision; mcp getPendingApproval, decideToolCall; pipeline beginTopic, resumeTopic, skipTopic, submitAnswer, resolveFounderFork; tickets validateLaneWriteScopes. Two were hand-verified rather than trusted: every non-test reference to runClaimLoop and gateDecision is a comment, and loop-claim.ts:223's own docstring says runClaimLoop's only callers are its own tests — the sentence admitting the defect was what concealed it. The strip now lives INSIDE countReferences rather than in its caller, because as a caller-side step the guarantee held only while every future caller remembered it, and a fixture written against the function passed while proving nothing.
$buriedExportsNote: W12-38, 2026-08-18: --max-buried 73 joins the same validator as a SECOND, separate ratchet. The W12-10 pass walks package BARRELS, so it can only see what a package publishes — and the instance that exposed the hole, runEscalationPolicy (the whole D-024 option-b escalation state machine, tested, called by nothing), is not in a barrel at all, so the validator confidently printed 43 gaps and never named it. That is the WORSE shape, not a lesser one: an uncalled export is reachable and unused, while an unexported implementation cannot be adopted without a separate barrel change, which is exactly how W12-04's packer, W12-09's code index and W12-37's pinned policy each sat dormant for waves. Calibration, measured not assumed: 90 raw -> 108 once comment text stopped counting as a call (loop-land-policy.ts names runEscalationPolicy twice in prose explaining why it deliberately does NOT call it, and the barrel pass's own doc admits this over-count) -> 73 once recorded fixtures and test-helper modules were excluded, since those are exported for tests and called by nothing else BY DESIGN under law 9a. Kept as a SEPARATE number rather than folded into --max: the two have different remedies (wire it up vs. wire it up AND export it), and merging would silently move the calibrated 43. KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: the barrel pass still counts prose mentions as calls, so its 43 is a floor, not a measurement — sharpening it would move a calibrated baseline for reasons unrelated to any ticket, and is filed as W12-39.
$visualGateNote: W13-07, 2026-08-18: the acceptance walker had written 21 frames on every run for waves and NOTHING ever compared them. That is how a UI reaches 'it looks horrible' with 42 style guards green — the guards check declarations, the frames checked nothing, and no gate closed the loop between them. Worse, found while building this: the walker itself had been broken since W12-36 renamed 'New Product', and again by W12-41's form change, because a capture script nothing runs stops working and says nothing. NO NEW DEPENDENCY: Playwright emits 8-bit truecolour non-interlaced PNG (verified from a real capture's IHDR), which node:zlib plus the five PNG filters decodes in ~60 lines; pixelmatch + pngjs would have been a TECH_STACK decision, and this repo ships five runtime dependencies on purpose. THRESHOLD MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: two captures of identical code showed 16 of 21 frames pixel-identical and a worst case of 0.21% (timestamps and generated project ids), so 0.5% is ~2.4x the floor while still failing on anything structural — the smallest real change in this wave moved several percent. Cost: ~17s to capture, under a second to compare. It writes to a temp dir via --out, because capturing into docs/acceptance/runs/ on every ticket would have added a megabyte of unread images per ticket. A DIFF IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT: an intended change is accepted BY NAME with --accept --ticket --reason, which records who changed the screen and why beside the baseline, rather than letting someone silently overwrite it.

Deliberately a NEW key, not a change to alwaysOk itself or globToRegex: the rest of alwaysOk (the board, the lockfile, tsconfig, ...) is genuinely modify-in-place infra and must keep exempting M/D.
